title: The solar cycle
summary: Sunspot counts rise and fall with the Sun's magnetic cycle; Fourier analysis finds its period, and polarity explains why 11 and 22 years.

concepts.label: Sunspot number
concepts.description: SILSO's international sunspot number, version 2, monthly and 13-month smoothed.

facts.text: Recalibrated in 2015 (version 2): the Wolf number's scale factor 0.6 was dropped and historic drifts corrected.

children.label: F10.7 radio flux
children.description: The Sun's 10.7 cm radio flux, measured since 1947; in the same file.

concepts.label: Solar cycle
concepts.description: One rise and fall of activity, minimum to minimum; numbered from 1755.

children.label: Cycle minimum
children.description: The lowest smoothed value; the start of a cycle.

children.label: Hale cycle
children.description: The 22-year magnetic cycle: the polarity of sunspot pairs flips each cycle.

children.label: Grand minimum
children.description: Decades of few spots (Maunder 1645–1715, before these data; Dalton around 1800).

concepts.label: Periodogram
concepts.description: Power of a series at each trial period: the squared Fourier sum.

facts.text: Schuster introduced the periodogram in 1898, to look for periodicities in sunspots and earthquakes.

concepts.label: Solar magnetic field
concepts.description: The dynamo field whose polarity flips at each maximum; measured on magnetograms.
